free_snapshot.text: free = np.maximum(w.free(), 0) on the post-diffusion pre-reaction state

free0.text: free0 = np.maximum(self.free(), 0)  -- computed ONCE at the top of _react, shared by the X and Y loop iterations

cand_Y.text: cand = np.minimum(self.n[res], free0), res = SY for the Y iteration

p_Y.text: p = np.minimum(1.0, kk*pair), kk=kY, pair = nX*nY

CALL_ORDER_IN_WorldOBTC._react.reading: pre_react runs BEFORE _react_core, on the identical state _react_core then reads; free in pre_react is w.free() == free0 in _react_core

EXACT_IDENTITY.claim: Q_recorded(t) == Q_reaction(t) exactly, per step, for the organiser cell
EXACT_IDENTITY.why: pre_react reads free = max(w.free(),0) and nSY, nX on the post-diffusion pre-reaction state; _react_core reads free0 = max(self.free(),0) and the same nSY, nX at the top of the same _react call. cand_Y = min(nSY, free) is the exact n-parameter of the Y-birth Binomial, and nX is the exact multiplier in p_Y = min(1, kY*nX*nY). No random number is drawn between pre_react and the Y binomial that changes nSY, nX or free.
EXACT_IDENTITY.per_step: the row is finalized in close_step every step; series has 11000 rows, so the Q ledger is NOT subsampled (stride 1)

PHASE.ONE_CAVEAT_FOR_MULTI_Y: Q_recorded = sum_cells nX*min(nSY,free). The engine's expected Y births per cell are min(nSY,free)*min(1, kY*nX*nY). In the unclamped one-Y-per-cell regime the expected intensity is kY * nX * min(nSY,free) = kY * Q_cell, so Q_recorded * kY is the exact expected first-birth intensity. With nY >= 2 in a cell the true intensity carries an extra factor nY that Q_recorded omits, and once p clamps, the linear relation breaks entirely. Q_recorded is therefore the exact ONE-Y unclamped exposure and nothing wider.

DEFINITIONS.Q_ORGANISER_t: nX * min(nSY, free) summed over cells with nY>0 (the original organiser location(s))
DEFINITIONS.Q_REACTION_t: the exact n*p-relevant exposure entering the Y-birth Binomial at the reaction sub-step
DEFINITIONS.Q_POSITION_t_x: nX(x) * min(nSY(x), free(x)) at an arbitrary cell x a Y particle could occupy
DEFINITIONS.Q_LINEAGE_t: Q_POSITION evaluated along a particular Y lineage's trajectory
DEFINITIONS.Q_AGGREGATE_t: sum over all cells currently containing Y
DEFINITIONS.Q_RECORDED_t: the scalar field 'Q' serialized by observe.py, index 20 of series

EQUALITIES_IN_THE_ONE_Y_BASELINE.Q_ORGANISER == Q_LINEAGE: True while the single Y sits at the organiser cell; at kY=0 (the archive) the Y never moves off its birth cell in the static branch and, in the mobile branch, the organiser IS the only Y, so Q_RECORDED tracks it
EQUALITIES_IN_THE_ONE_Y_BASELINE.Q_ORGANISER == Q_AGGREGATE: True while there is exactly one Y cell

WHERE_THEY_DIVERGE_AFTER_THE_FIRST_BIRTH.Q_RECORDED_vs_Q_REACTION: diverge if two Y become co-located: Q_RECORDED omits the nY multiplier in p_Y
WHERE_THEY_DIVERGE_AFTER_THE_FIRST_BIRTH.Q_ORGANISER_vs_Q_POSITION: diverge as soon as a mobile descendant leaves the organiser cell: the exposure at the descendant's new cell is a DIFFERENT, unrecorded quantity
WHERE_THEY_DIVERGE_AFTER_THE_FIRST_BIRTH.Q_ORGANISER_vs_Q_AGGREGATE: diverge once there are two Y cells
WHERE_THEY_DIVERGE_AFTER_THE_FIRST_BIRTH.LOAD_BEARING: the recorded field is the same object as PMCR01's one-organiser Q derivation. That does NOT make it the two-Y lineage environment. Q_POSITION and Q_LINEAGE for a separated descendant are never recorded per step.
